title: REPEAT OFFENDER SENTENCED TO PRISON
full_story:
Clay County State’s Attorney Phillip M. Givens has announced that Henry J. Dietz, 65, of Louisville, Illinois, was sentenced to time in the Illinois Department of Corrections on September 28, 2026, in Clay County Circuit Court for violating the terms and conditions of conditional discharge.

Dietz was previously placed on 24 months of conditional discharge for Unlawful Possession of Methamphetamine, a Class 3 Felony, on June 9, 2025. He was ordered not to violate any criminal statute or ordinance of any jurisdiction. He violated his conditional discharge by committing a new Unlawful Possession of Methamphetamine offense in Clay County. Dietz was found guilty of the violation on August 12, 2026. After a contested sentencing hearing on September 28, 2026, Dietz was sentenced to 7 years in the Illinois Department of Corrections by Judge Joel Powless. Dietz will have a 6-month period of Mandatory Supervised Release to follow.

The case was investigated by the Clay County Sheriff’s Office. State’s Attorney Phillip Givens said: “My office continues to hold offenders accountable for violating terms and conditions of the Court. We want offenders to become productive members of the community, but if they do not abide by the Court’s terms and conditions, then there will be repercussions. I commend our local law enforcement for their hard work and cooperation in holding people accountable.”

title: DID EFFINGHAM POLICE DISCOVER A BOMB?
full_story:
Effingham City Police are looking into a suspicious item its officers discovered during a traffic stop over the weekend.

When officers pulled the vehicle over, they noticed an unusual device in the rear seat.  The driver now faces multiple charges and police are trying to determine if the item they found is a bomb.

They took 30-year-old Cody Welch of Teutopolis into custody, and he now faces charges including DUI, unlawful possession of a weapon and ammunition by a felon, possession of methamphetamine and possession of a controlled substance.  Welch has since been released and should make his initial court appearance this week in Effingham County Circuit Court.

Effingham Police have not yet learned whether the item recovered is a bomb or not.  The Illinois Secretary of State Police Bomb Squad  were called in and they’re tasked with determining what exactly the device is and expect to release their results later in the week.

title: USDA CROP PROGRESS AND CONDTION REPORT
full_story:
Five inches of rainfall last week and up to 3 more inches in the forecast this week are keeping fields and crops very wet in parts of northern Illinois.  That being said,  Harvest progress in Illinois remains ahead of average pace.

In its latest crop progress and condition report released Monday, USDA estimated 6% of the state’s wheat is planted with 1% emerged. According to the USDA, there were 5.3 days suitable for fieldwork in the week ending September 27th.

Topsoil moisture supply was rated 11% very short, 22% short, 60% adequate and 7% surplus. Subsoil moisture supply was rated 11% very short, 26% short, 59% adequate, and 4% surplus.

Corn dented reached 97%, compared to the 5-year average of 94%. Corn mature reached 83%, compared to the 5-year average of 77%. Corn harvested reached 26%, compared to the 5-year average of 17%. Corn condition was rated 4% very poor, 8% poor, 28% fair, 45% good, and 15% excellent.

Soybeans dropping leaves reached 79%, compared to the 5-year average of 79%. Soybeans harvested reached 21%, compared to the 5-year average of 14%. Soybean condition was rated 4% very poor, 7% poor, 29% fair, 46% good, and 14% excellent.

Meanwhile, winter wheat planting is a bit behind to start the season. USDA estimates 6% has been planted in Illinois compared to 11% at the same time last year and 8% on average. Emergence was unchanged from last week at 1%. Nationally, 27% is planted compared to the average 34%.

title: STATE POLICE REMINDS MOTORISTS HARVEST CONTINUES
full_story:
Illinois State Police reminds everyone and urges drivers and farmers to share the road as the fall harvest season continues.

Troopers warn of the high number of slow-moving machinery and vehicles traveling between fields on public roads. Illinois Department of Transportation data recorded 275 crashes involving farm tractors or equipment statewide in 2024.

State police advise drivers to reduce speeds, increase following distance behind wide machinery, and watch for amber flashing lights and slow-moving vehicle emblems. Passing is prohibited in no-passing zones and within 100 feet of intersections, railroad crossings, and bridges. Drivers should also watch for hand signals from farmers driving older equipment without turn indicators.  Also beware of harvest machinery and loaded grain trucks turning onto the highway and needing time to get up to highway speed.

Authorities also ask farmers to avoid traveling during peak traffic hours, bad weather, or after dark when possible. Operators should ensure all lights and reflectors are clear of dust and field debris and safely pull onto shoulders when feasible to allow backed-up traffic to pass.

title: FLORA ELKS FREE ORTHOPEDIC CLINIC
full_story:
The Flora Elks 1659 and Olney Elks 926 Lodges in cooperation with the Illinois Elks Children’s Care Corporation are sponsoring their next free children’s orthopedic assessment clinic.  It’s scheduled for Wednesday, November 4, 2026.  The clinic is set to start at 11:30am and you must make an appointment to attend.

Parents should call to schedule their child’s appointment and call the Illinois Elks Children’s Care office at 1-800-272-0074 between the hours of 9:00am and 4:00pm Monday through Friday.  Keep in mind that there are no charges for the services available at this clinic and no medical referral is necessary.

The Elks Orthopedic Clinic is coming to the Flora Medical Clinic on the campus of Clay County Hospital at 292 Stacey Burk Drive in Flora on Wednesday, November 4th.  Dr. Julko Fullop is the physician.

title: EFFECTIVELY ANTICIPATING DISASTERS
full_story:
Planning for the worst is not a fun thing to do, but it can help make a bad situation a little easier to deal with.  That’s what mitigation is all about.  These mitigation projects can reduce injuries and fatalities when mother nature roars or when other unexpected events cause havoc and destruction.  Maintaining vital services for the residents of Clay County is the main topic at the Clay County Hazard Mitigation Planning Committee meeting.  It’s scheduled for Wednesday, October 7th at the Clay County Health Department, on E. 12th Street, in Flora starting at 1:00 pm.

The Committee began work in January to update the county’s Natural Hazards Mitigation Plan.  The plan details past severe weather events that impacted Clay County and identifies mitigation projects and activities that can be taken before an event occurs to protect residents along with critical services and infrastructure.

Flora-Clay County Emergency and Disaster Services Coordinator Steve Lewis says, getting FEMA’s approval of an updated Plan  makes all participants eligible to apply for federal grant money specifically for mitigation projects and activities.

Building community safe rooms, acquiring flood prone properties, resolving drainage issues, retrofitting critical infrastructure to better withstand hazard events, installing back-up power supplies, and developing public information materials are just a few of the mitigation projects commonly proposed in Illinois.

Projects identified by members at the upcoming meeting become part of the County’s updated Plan.  While the committee provides input on portions of the Plan, look for a full public presentation that encourages review and seeks comments before it is submitted to the state and federal government for approval.

Steve Lewis adds to expect a public forum after the first of the year for local residents to review the update and ask questions of Committee Members.  A two-week public comment period follows the public forum to accommodate people who are unable to attend.  He says they want to make sure any interested party has an opportunity to review and comment on the draft Plan update.

You can submit questions and comments to the Flora-Clay County Emergency Services and Disaster Agency office.  Contact Steve Lewis at (618) 662-8211 or via email at [email protected].  His office is at 744 East North Avenue, next to Rotary Park.

title: CHESTER BRIDGE IMPLOSION
full_story:
Capital News Illinois and the Saluki Local Report Lab report that hundreds of people gathered along the riverfront Monday morning to watch the 80-year-old Chester Bridge come down.

Explosives ripped through the old bridge, sending it crashing into the Mississippi River as cheers rose from the crowd. A piece of local history had disappeared, marking the end of one era and the beginning of another for the crossing between Illinois and Missouri.

Demolition crews used strategically placed explosives to bring the bridge straight down and keep the collapse within a controlled area. Crews will now work to remove the remaining pieces of the old bridge from the river.

The old bridge has been replaced by the $307.1 million Don Welge Memorial Bridge, a joint Missouri-Illinois-federal project named for the late Gilster-Mary Lee corporation president and CEO, who pushed for years for a safer replacement.  The video of the bridge coming down can be found on You Tube. and you can link to it at wnoi.com.

Daylin Williams and Adam Gunther reported from Chester Monday morning for the Saluki Local Reporting Lab and Capitol News Illinois.

title: WEBB GRADUATES FBI ACADEMY
full_story:
An Effingham Police Officer earned a national distinction earlier this month and has the opportunity to put his newfound knowledge to work for the citizens  he is sworn to protect.

Effingham Deputy Police Chief Tom Webb was one of the graduates of this elite class.  Webb was one of 256 law enforcement professionals to graduate on September 17th, from the FBI National Academy in Quantico, Virginia.

The National Academy taught men and women from 44 states and the District of Columbia and included 29 international members from 28 countries.  It offers 10 weeks of advanced communication, leadership, and fitness training for professionals with proven records and results.  On average, officers have 21 years of law enforcement experience and usually return to their agencies to serve in executive level positions.

During training FBI Academy instructors, special agents, and other staff with advanced degrees provide the training from instructors who are recognized internationally in their fields.

FBI Director Kash Patel delivered remarks at the ceremony.  Since 1972, National Academy students earn undergraduate and graduate credits from the University of Virginia, which accredits all the National Academy courses.

The FBI National Academy is the same facility where the FBI trains its special agents and intelligence analysts.  Deputy Chief Webb notes that The FBI National Academy was an incredible experience, both professionally and personally, giving him the opportunity to learn alongside law-enforcement leaders from across the country, exchange ideas and perspectives, and bring those experiences back with him, is something he’ll  carry throughout his career.  He’s grateful for the experience and everything he learned.  He’s happy to be home with family and back in the community that he’s proud to serve.  Webb adds that he’s looking forward to take what he’s learned at the National Academy to work for the Effingham Police Department as he continues  to serve the people of Effingham.

title: I-CASH AUCTION
full_story:
A 1926 British Sovereign gold coin bearing the image of King George V, three Egyptian leather jewelry boxes, and baseball cards of Chicago legends Ryne Sandberg and Frank Thomas are among the treasures available at the online I-CASH auction that runs through Sunday.

Illinois State Treasurer Michael Frerichs, whose office oversees unclaimed property in Illinois, says, “Our online auction offers a variety of distinctive, memorable items you can buy for yourself, a friend, or a loved one.  If there’s a collector in your life, or a certain someone who’s hard to shop for, you can find great gifts like vintage jewelry, collectible coins, and classic baseball cards of outstanding players.”

Other auction items include; a 1986 American Eagle gold coin, a 14-karat yellow gold pendant with an opal, a 10-karat yellow gold ring with pearls, an Engelhard 10-ounce .999 fine silver bar, baseball cards of Hall of Famers Ernie Banks, Greg Maddux, Stan Musial, Nolan Ryan and others, $1 silver certificates from 1935 and 1957, and Morgan silver dollars from the late 1800’s and early 1900’s.

You can view all auction items in the catalog on the HiBid website.

Prospective bidders first must sign up on HiBid and create an account.

The Illinois State Treasurer’s Office is the custodian of unclaimed property, including lost bank accounts, insurance policy proceeds, unpaid rebate cards, and the contents of safe deposit boxes.  Items are surrendered to the Treasurer’s Office after private entities have tried to locate the owner for several years.

The Treasurer’s Office also holds an annual in-person auction of unclaimed property during the Illinois State Fair in August.  The 2026 in-person auction generated total sales of $397,475.  All auction proceeds will be held for the rightful owners, no matter how long it takes.

An estimated one-in-four adults in Illinois who search the state’s unclaimed property website, also known as I-CASH, find missing money that should be returned to them.  Visit the I-CASH website at icash.illinoistreasurer.gov/  to find out if any missing money is waiting for you.
